The SNF claim must include two data items derived from the MDS assessment: 

###### **Assessment Reference Date (ARD)** 

The ARD must be reported on the SNF claim. CMS has developed internal mechanisms to link the MDS assessment and the claims processing system. 

###### **Health Insurance Prospective Payment System (HIPPS) Code** 

Each SNF claim contains a five-position HIPPS code for the purpose of billing Part A covered days to the Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC). The HIPPS code consists of a series of codes representing the resident’s PDPM classification and the Assessment Indicator (AI) as described below. CMS provides standard software and logic for HIPPS code calculation. 

###### **PDPM Classification** 

The first four positions of the HIPPS code contain the PDPM classification codes for each PDPM component to be billed for Medicare reimbursement. The PDPM classification is calculated from the MDS assessment clinical data. See Section 6.6 for calculation details on each PDPM group. CMS provides standard software, development tools, and logic for PDPM calculation. CMS software, or private software developed with the CMS data specifications, is used to encode and transmit the MDS assessment data and automatically calculates the resident’s PDPM classification. CMS edits and validates the PDPM classification code of transmitted MDS assessments. Skilled nursing facilities are not permitted to submit Medicare Part A claims until the assessments have been accepted into the CMS database, and they must use the PDPM classification code as validated by CMS when bills are filed, except in cases in which the facility must bill the default code (ZZZZZ). See Section 6.8 for details.

**CH 6: Medicare SNF PPS** 

The PDPM HIPPS code is recorded on the MDS 3.0 in item Z0100A (Medicare Part A HIPPS code). The HIPPS code included on the SNF claim depends on the specific type of assessment involved (as described below). 

The HIPPS code in item Z0100A is validated by CMS when the assessment is submitted. If the submitted code is incorrect, the validation report will include a warning giving the correct code; the facility must enter this correct code in the HIPPS code item on the bill. 

The provider must ensure that all PPS assessment requirements are met. When the provider fails to meet the PPS assessment requirements, such as when the assessment is late (as evidenced by a late ARD), the provider may be required to bill the default code. In these situations, the provider is responsible to ensure that the default code and not the PDPM classification-based HIPPS code validated by CMS in item Z0100A is billed for the applicable number of days. See Section 6.8 of this chapter for greater detail. 

###### **AI Code** 

The last position of the HIPPS code represents the AI, identifying the assessment type. The AI coding system indicates the different types of assessments that define different PPS payment periods and is based on the coding of item A0310B. CMS provides standard software, development tools, and logic for AI code calculation. CMS software, or private software developed with the CMS tools, automatically calculates the AI code. The AI code is validated by CMS when the assessment is submitted. If the submitted AI code is incorrect on the assessment, the validation report will include a warning and provide the correct code. The facility must enter this correct AI code in the HIPPS code item on the bill. The code consists of one digit, which is defined below. In situations when the provider is to bill the default code, the AI provided on the validation report is to be used along with the default code, ZZZZZ, on the SNF claim. 

Refer to the **Medicare Claims Processing Manual** , Chapter 6, for detailed claims processing requirements and policies. 

The AI code identifies the assessment used to establish the per diem payment rate for the standard PPS payment periods. These assessments are the 5-Day assessment and Interim Payment Assessment. Table 5 displays the AI code for each of the PPS assessment types and the standard payment period for each assessment type.

|**AI Code**|**Assessment Type (abbreviation)**|**Standard Payment**<br>**Period**|
|---|---|---|

|||Section 2.9|

**CH 6: Medicare SNF PPS** 

###### **6.5 SNF PPS Eligibility Criteria** 

Under SNF PPS, beneficiaries must meet the established eligibility requirements for a Part A SNF-level stay. These requirements are summarized in this section. Refer to the **Medicare General Information, Eligibility, and Entitlement Manual** , Chapter 1 (Pub. 100-1), and the **Medicare Benefit Policy Manual** , Chapter 8 (Pub. 100-2), for detailed SNF coverage requirements and policies. 

###### **Technical Eligibility Requirements** 

The beneficiary must meet the following criteria: 

- Beneficiary is enrolled in Medicare Part A and has days available to use. 

- There has been a three-day prior qualifying hospital stay (i.e., three midnights). 

- Admission for SNF-level services is within 30 days of discharge from an acute care stay or within 30 days of discharge from a SNF level of care. 

###### **Clinical Eligibility Requirements** 

A beneficiary is eligible for SNF extended care if all of the following requirements are met: 

- The beneficiary has a need for and receives medically necessary skilled care on a daily basis, which is provided by or under the direct supervision of skilled nursing or rehabilitation professionals. 

- As a practical matter, these skilled services can only be provided in an SNF. 

- The services provided must be for a condition: 

   - for which the resident was treated during the qualifying hospital stay, or 

   - that arose while the resident was in the SNF for treatment of a condition for which they were previously treated in a hospital. 

###### **Physician Certification** 

The attending physician or a physician on the staff of the skilled nursing facility who has knowledge of the case—or a nurse practitioner (NP), physician assistant (PA), or clinical nurse specialist (CNS) who does not have a direct or indirect employment relationship with the facility but who is working in collaboration with the physician—must certify and then periodically recertify the need for extended care services in the skilled nursing facility. 

- **Certifications** are required at the time of admission or as soon thereafter as is reasonable and practicable (42 CFR 424.20). The initial certification 

   - affirms, per the required content found in 42 CFR 424.20, that the resident meets the existing SNF level of care definition, or 

**October 2025** 

**Page 6-10** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**CH 6: Medicare SNF PPS** 

   - validates via written statement that the resident’s assignment to one of the upper PDPM groups (defined below) is correct. 

      - Those nursing groups encompassed by the Extensive Services, Special Care High, Special Care Low, and Clinically Complex nursing categories; 

      - PT and OT groups TA, TB, TC, TD, TE, TF, TG, TJ, TK, TN, and TO; 

      - SLP groups SC, SE, SF, SH, SI, SJ, SK, and SL; and 

      - The NTA component’s uppermost (12+) comorbidity group. 

- **Re-certifications** are used to document the continued need for skilled extended care services. 

   - The first re-certification is required no later than the 14th day of the SNF stay. 

   - Subsequent re-certifications are required at no later than 30-day intervals after the date of the first re-certification. 

   - The initial certification and first re-certification may be signed at the same time. 

###### **6.6 PDPM Calculation Worksheet for SNFs** 

In the PDPM, there are five case-mix adjusted components: PT, OT, SLP, NTA, and Nursing. Each resident is to be classified into one and only one group for each of the five case-mix adjusted components. In other words, each resident is classified into a PT group, an OT group, an SLP group, an NTA group, and a nursing group. For each of the case-mix adjusted components, there are a number of groups to which a resident may be assigned, based on the relevant MDS 3.0 data for that component. There are 16 PT groups, 16 OT groups, 12 SLP groups, 6 NTA groups, and 25 nursing groups. 

PDPM classifies residents into a separate group for each of the case-mix adjusted components, each of which has its own associated case-mix indexes and base rates. Additionally, PDPM applies variable per diem payment adjustments to three components, PT, OT, and NTA, to account for changes in resource use over a stay. The adjusted PT, OT, and NTA per diem rates are then added together with the unadjusted SLP and nursing component rates and the non-casemix component to determine the full per diem rate for a given resident.

##### **Calculation of PDPM Co nitive Level** **<u>g</u>** 

The PDPM cognitive level is utilized in the SLP payment component of PDPM. One of four PDPM cognitive performance levels is assigned based on the Brief Interview for Mental Status (BIMS) or the Staff Assessment for Mental Status for the PDPM cognitive level. If neither the BIMS nor the staff assessment for the PDPM cognitive level is complete, then the resident will be classified as if the resident is cognitively intact. 

###### **STEP #1** 

Determine the resident’s BIMS Summary Score on the MDS 3.0 based on the resident interview. Instructions for completing the BIMS are in Chapter 3, Section C. The BIMS involves the following items: 

C0200 Repetition of three words C0300 Temporal orientation C0400 Recall 

Item C0500 provides a BIMS Summary Score that ranges from 00 to 15. If the resident interview is not successful, then the BIMS Summary Score will equal 99. 

Calculate the resident’s PDPM cognitive level using the following mapping: 

**Table 6: Calculation of PDPM Level from BIMS** 

|**PDPM Cognitive Level**|**BIMS Score**|
|---|---|
|Cognitively Intact|13-15|
|Mildly Impaired|8-12|
|Moderately Impaired|0-7|
|SeverelyImpaired|-|



###### **PDPM Cognitive Level: __________** 

If the resident’s Summary Score is 99 (resident interview not successful) or the Summary Score is blank (resident interview not attempted and skipped) or the Summary Score has a dash value (not assessed), then proceed to Step #2 to use the Staff Assessment for Mental Status for the PDPM cognitive level. 

###### **STEP #2** 

If the resident’s Summary Score is 99 or the Summary Score is blank or has a dash value, then determine the resident’s cognitive status based on the Staff Assessment for Mental Status for the PDPM cognitive level using the following steps: 

**October 2025** 

**Page 6-12** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**CH 6: Medicare SNF PPS** 

- A) The resident classifies as severely impaired if one of the following conditions exists: 

   - a. Comatose (B0100 = 1) and completely dependent or activity did not occur at admission (GG0130A1, GG0130C1, GG0170B1, GG0170C1, GG0170D1, GG0170E1, and GG0170F1 all equal 01, 09, or 88). It should be noted that, in the case of an IPA, the items used for calculation of the resident’s PDPM functional score are the Interim Performance items (GG0XXXX5), rather than the Admission Performance items (GG0XXXX1). For example, rather than GG0130B1, which is used on the 5-Day to assess the resident’s Oral Hygiene Admission Performance, the IPA uses item GG0130B5 in order to measure the resident’s Oral Hygiene Interim Performance. 

   - b. Severely impaired cognitive skills for daily decision making (C1000 = 3). 

- B) If the resident is not severely impaired based on Step A, then determine the resident’s Basic Impairment Count and Severe Impairment Count. 

For each of the conditions below that applies, add one to the Basic Impairment Count. 

- a. In Cognitive Skills for Daily Decision Making, the resident has modified independence or is moderately impaired (C1000 = 1 or 2). 

- b. In Makes Self Understood, the resident is usually understood, sometimes understood, or rarely/never understood (B0700 = 1, 2, or 3). 

- c. Based on the Staff Assessment for Mental Status, the resident has a memory problem (C0700 = 1). 

Sum a., b., and c. to get the Basic Impairment Count: _____ 

For each of the conditions below that applies, add one to the Severe Impairment Count. 

- a. In Cognitive Skills for Daily Decision Making, the resident is moderately impaired (C1000 = 2). 

- b. In Makes Self Understood, the resident is sometimes understood or rarely/never understood (B0700 = 2 or 3). 

Sum a. and b. to get the Severe Impairment Count: _____ 

- C) The resident classifies as moderately impaired if the Severe Impairment Count is 1 or 2 and the Basic Impairment Count is 2 or 3. 

- D) The resident classifies as mildly impaired if the Basic Impairment Count is 1 and the Severe Impairment Count is 0, 1, or 2, or if the Basic Impairment Count is 2 or 3 and the Severe Impairment Count is 0. 

- E) The resident classifies as cognitively intact if both the Severe Impairment Count and Basic Impairment Count are 0. 

**PDPM Cognitive Level: __________**

Some ICD-10-CM codes can map to a different clinical category from the default depending on a resident’s prior inpatient procedure history. For these codes, a resident may be categorized into a surgical clinical category if the resident received a surgical procedure during the prior inpatient stay that relates to the primary reason for the Part A SNF stay as indicated by item J2100. To do so, refer to the PDPM Clinical Categories to ICD-10 _-_ Diagnosis Codes mapping (available at _<u>https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/prospective payment-systems/skilled-nursing-facility-snf/patient-driven-model</u>_ <u>), which maps a resident’s</u> primary diagnosis as recorded in MDS item I0020B to the 10 PDPM primary diagnosis clinical categories.

Some ICD-10-CM codes can map to a different clinical category from the default depending on a resident’s prior inpatient procedure history. For these codes, a resident may be categorized into a surgical clinical category if the resident received a surgical procedure during the prior inpatient stay that relates to the primary reason for the Part A SNF stay as indicated by item J2100. If the PDPM clinical category mapping indicates that the resident’s primary diagnosis code is eligible for one of the two orthopedic surgery categories (major joint replacement or spinal surgery, and orthopedic surgery (except major joint replacement or spinal surgery)), then proceed to Step 1A; if eligible for the non-orthopedic surgery category, then proceed to Step 1C. Otherwise, proceed to Step 1D to finalize the primary diagnosis clinical category assignment.

###### **STEP #1**

2. Determine whether the resident meets the criteria for the comorbidity: “Parenteral/IV Feeding – High Intensity” or the comorbidity: “Parenteral/IV Feeding – Low Intensity.” To do so, first determine if the resident received parenteral/IV feeding during the last 7 days while a resident of the SNF using item K0520A3. If the resident did not receive parenteral/IV feeding during the last 7 days while a resident, then the resident does not meet the criteria for Parenteral/IV Feeding – High Intensity or Parenteral/IV Feeding – Low Intensity. 

If the resident did receive parenteral/IV feeding during the last 7 days while a resident, then use item K0710A to determine if the proportion of total calories the resident received through parenteral or tube feeding was 51% or more while a resident (K0710A2 = 3). If K0710A2 = 3, then the resident meets the criteria for Parenteral/IV Feeding – High Intensity. If the proportion of total calories the resident received through parenteral or tube feeding was 2650% (K0710A2 = 2) and average fluid intake per day by IV or tube feeding was 501 cc per day or more while a resident (K0710B2 = 2), then the resident qualifies for Parenteral/IV Feeding – Low Intensity.

Finally, round this sum to the nearest integer. This is the **PDPM Function Score for nursing payment** . The PDPM Function Score for nursing payment ranges from 0 through 16. 

###### **<u>PDPM NURSING FUNCTION SCORE:</u> _____** 

###### **STEP #2** 

Determine the resident’s nursing case-mix group using the hierarchical classification below. Nursing classification under PDPM employs the hierarchical classification method. Hierarchical classification is used in some payment systems, in staffing analysis, and in many research projects. In the hierarchical approach, start at the top and work down through the PDPM nursing classification model steps discussed below; the assigned classification is the first group for which the resident qualifies. In other words, start with the Extensive Services groups at the top of the PDPM nursing classification model. Then go down through the groups in hierarchical order: Extensive Services, Special Care High, Special Care Low, Clinically Complex, Behavioral Symptoms and Cognitive Performance, and Reduced Physical Function. When you find the first of the 25 individual PDPM nursing groups for which the resident qualifies, assign that group as the PDPM nursing classification. 

- 1 Calculate the sum of the Function Scores for Sit to Lying and Lying to Sitting on Side of Bed. Divide this sum by 2. This is the Average Bed Mobility Function Score. 

- 2 Calculate the sum of the Function Scores for Sit to Stand, Chair/Bed-to-Chair, and Toilet Transfer. Divide by 3. This is the Average Transfer Function Score.

##### **CATEGORY: BEHAVIORAL SYMPTOMS AND COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE** 

Classification in this category is based on the presence of certain behavioral symptoms or the resident’s cognitive performance. Use the following instructions: 

###### **STEP #1** 

Determine the resident’s PDPM Nursing Function Score. If the resident's PDPM Nursing Function Score is 11 or greater, go to Step #2. 

**If the PDPM Nursing Function Score is less than 11, skip to the Reduced Physical Function Category now.** 

###### **STEP #2** 

**If the resident interview using the Brief Interview for Mental Status (BIMS) was not conducted (indicated by a value of “0” for item C0100), skip the remainder of this step and proceed to Step #3 to check staff assessment for cognitive impairment.** 

Determine the resident’s cognitive status based on resident interview using the BIMS. Instructions for completing the BIMS are in Chapter 3, Section C. The BIMS items involve the following: 

C0200 Repetition of three words C0300 Temporal orientation C0400 Recall 

Item C0500 provides a BIMS Summary Score for these items and indicates the resident’s cognitive performance, with a score of 15 indicating the best cognitive performance and 0 indicating the worst performance. If the resident interview is not successful, then the BIMS Summary Score will equal 99. 

**If the resident’s Summary Score is less than or equal to 9, they classify in the Behavioral Symptoms and Cognitive Performance category. Skip to Step #5** . 

**If the resident’s Summary Score is greater than 9 but not 99, proceed to Step #4 to check behavioral symptoms.** 

**If the resident’s Summary Score is 99 (resident interview not successful) or the Summary Score is blank (resident interview not attempted and skipped) or the Summary Score has a dash value (not assessed), proceed to Step #3 to check staff assessment for cognitive impairment.** 

**October 2025** 

**Page 6-44** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**CH 6: Medicare SNF PPS** 

###### **STEP #3** 

Determine the resident’s cognitive status based on the staff assessment rather than on resident interview. 

Check if **one** of the three following conditions exists: 

1.  B0100 Coma (B0100 = 1) and completely dependent or activity did not occur at admission (GG0130A1, GG0130C1, GG0170B1, GG0170C1, GG0170D1, GG0170E1, and GG0170F1 all equal 01, 09, or 88) 

2.  C1000 Severely impaired cognitive skills for daily decision making (C1000 = 3) 

3.  B0700, C0700, C1000 Two or more of the following impairment indicators are present: B0700 > 0 Usually, sometimes, or rarely/never understood C0700 = 1 Short-term memory problem C1000 > 0 Impaired cognitive skills for daily decision making **and** One or more of the following severe impairment indicators are present: B0700 >= 2 Sometimes or rarely/never makes self understood C1000 >= 2 Moderately or severely impaired cognitive skills for daily decision making 

**If the resident meets one of the three above conditions, then they classify in Behavioral Symptoms and Cognitive Performance. Skip to Step #5. If they do not meet any of the three conditions, proceed to Step #4.** 

###### **STEP #4** 

Determine whether the resident presents with **one** of the following behavioral symptoms: 

|E0100A|Hallucinations|
|---|---|
|E0100B|Delusions|
|E0200A|Physical behavioral symptoms directed toward others (2 or 3)|
|E0200B|Verbal behavioral symptoms directed toward others (2 or 3)|
|E0200C|Other behavioral symptoms not directed toward others (2 or 3)|
|E0800|Rejection of care (2 or 3)|
|E0900|Wandering (2 or 3)|



**If the resident presents with one of the symptoms above, then they classify in Behavioral Symptoms and Cognitive Performance. Proceed to Step #5. If they do not present with behavioral symptoms, skip to the Reduced Physical Function Category.**

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**CH 6: Medicare SNF PPS** 

###### **STEP #5** 

###### **Determine Restorative Nursing Count**

##### **Calculation of Variable Per Diem Pa ment Ad ustment** **<u>y j</u>** 

PDPM incorporates variable per diem payment adjustments to account for changes in resource use over the course of a stay for three payment components: PT, OT, and NTA. To calculate the per diem rate for these components, multiply the component base rate by the case-mix index associated with the resident’s case-mix group and the adjustment factor based on the day of the stay, as shown in the following equation: 

_Component Per Diem Payment = Component Base Rate x Resident Group CMI x Component Adjustment Factor_ 

The adjustment factors for the PT and OT components can be found in the table below. 

**Table 20: PT and OT Variable Per Diem Adjustment Factors** 

|**Day in Stay**|**PT and OT Adjustment Factor**|
|---|---|
|1-20|1.00|
|21-27|0.98|
|28-34|0.96|
|35-41|0.94|
|42-48|0.92|
|49-55|0.90|
|56-62|0.88|
|63-69|0.86|
|70-76|0.84|
|77-83|0.82|
|84-90|0.80|
|91-97|0.78|
|98-100|0.76|



The adjustment factors for the NTA component can be found in the table below. 

**Table 21: NTA Variable Per Diem Adjustment Factors** 

|**Day in Stay**|**NTA Adjustment Factor**|
|---|---|
|1-3|3.00|
|4-100|1.00|

**CH 6: Medicare SNF PPS** 

##### **Calculation of Total Case-Mix Adjusted PDPM Per Diem Rate** 

The total case-mix adjusted PDPM per diem rate equals the sum of each of the five case-mix adjusted components and the non-case-mix adjusted rate component. To calculate the total casemix adjusted per diem rate, add all component per diem rates calculated in prior steps together, along with the non-case-mix rate component, as shown in the following equation: 

_Total Case-Mix Adjusted Per Diem Payment = (PT Component Per Diem Rate * PT Variable Per Diem Adjustment Factor) + (OT Component Per Diem Rate * OT Variable Per Diem Adjustment Factor) + SLP Component Per Diem Rate + (NTA Component Per Diem Rate * NTA Variable Per Diem Adjustment Factor) + Nursing Component Per Diem Rate + Non-Case-Mix Component Per Diem Rate_

**CH 6: Medicare SNF PPS** 

###### **6.7 SNF PPS Policies** 

Requirements and policies for SNF PPS are described in greater detail in Chapter 8 of the **Medicare Benefit Policy Manual** <u>(https://www.cms.gov/Regulations-andGuidance/Guidance/Manuals/downloads/bp102c08pdf.pdf). There are some situations that the</u> SNF may encounter that may impact Medicare Part A SNF coverage for a resident, affect the PPS assessment schedule, or impact the reimbursement received by the SNF. 

###### **Delay in Requiring and Receiving Skilled Services (30-Day Transfer)** 

There are instances in which the resident does not require SNF level of care services when initially admitted to the SNF. When the resident requires and receives SNF level of care services within 30 days from the hospital discharge, Day 1 for the PPS assessment schedule is the day on which SNF level of care services begin. For example, if a resident is discharged from the hospital on August 1 and the SNF determines on August 30 that the resident requires skilled service for a condition that was treated during the qualifying hospital stay, then the SNF would start the PPS assessment schedule with a 5-Day PPS assessment, with August 30 as Day 1 for scheduling purposes. However, if the resident requires and receives a SNF level of care 31 or more days after the hospital discharge, the resident does not qualify for a SNF Part A stay (see Medical Appropriateness Exception below). 

###### **Medical Appropriateness Exception (Deferred Treatment)** 

An elapsed period of more than 30 days is permitted for starting SNF Part A services when a resident’s condition makes it inappropriate to begin an active course of treatment in a SNF immediately after a qualifying hospital stay discharge. It is applicable only where, under accepted medical practice, the established pattern of treatment for a particular condition indicates that a covered level of SNF care will be required within a predeterminable time frame, and it is medically predictable at the time of hospital discharge that the resident will require SNF level of care within a predetermined time period (for more detailed information see Chapter 8 of the **Medicare Benefit Policy Manual** ). For example, a resident is admitted to the SNF after a qualifying hospital stay for an open reduction and internal fixation of a hip. It is determined upon hospital discharge that the resident is not ready for weight-bearing activity but will most likely be ready in 4-6 weeks. The physician writes an order to start therapy when the resident is able to tolerate weight bearing. Once the resident is able to start therapy, the Medicare Part A stay begins, and the 5-Day assessment will be performed. Day 1 of the stay will be the first day on which the resident starts therapy services. 

###### **Interrupted Stay** 

An “interrupted” SNF stay is defined as one in which a resident is discharged from SNF care and subsequently readmitted to the same SNF (not a different SNF) within 3 days or less after the discharge (the “interruption window”). 

The interruption window is a 3-day period, starting with the calendar day of Part A discharge and including the 2 immediately following calendar days, ending at midnight. In other words, the resident must return to the same SNF by 11:59 p.m. at the end of the third calendar day. The 

**October 2025** 

**Page 6-50** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**CH 6: Medicare SNF PPS** 

interruption window begins on the first non-covered day following a Part A-covered stay and ends at 11:59 p.m. on the third consecutive non-covered day following a Part A-covered stay. 

If both conditions are met, the subsequent stay is considered a continuation of the previous Medicare Part A stay for the purposes of both the variable per diem schedule and the assessment schedule. The variable per diem schedule continues from the day of the previous discharge. For example, if the resident was discharged on Day 7, payment rates resume at Day 7 upon readmission. The assessment schedule also continues from the day of the previous discharge. Thus, no new 5-Day assessment is required upon the subsequent readmission, although the optional IPA may be completed at clinician’s discretion. 

If a resident is readmitted to the same SNF more than 3 consecutive calendar days after discharge, OR in any instance when the resident is admitted to a different SNF (regardless of the length of time between stays), then the Interrupted Stay Policy does not apply, and the subsequent stay is considered a new stay. In such cases, the variable per diem schedule resets to Day 1 payment rates, and the assessment schedule also resets to Day 1, necessitating the completion of a new 5-Day assessment. 

Example 1: Resident A is admitted to the SNF on 11/07/19. They are admitted to a hospital on 11/20/19. They return to the same SNF on 11/25/19. Because Resident A is readmitted to the same SNF more than three calendar days after discharge, this would be considered a new stay. The assessment schedule would be reset to Day 1, beginning with a new 5-Day assessment, and the variable per diem schedule would begin from Day 1. 

Example 2: Resident B is admitted to the SNF on 11/07/19. They are admitted to the hospital on 11/20/19. They are admitted to a different SNF on 11/22/19. Because Resident B is admitted to a different SNF, this would be considered a new stay. The assessment schedule would be reset, beginning with a new 5-Day assessment, and the variable per diem schedule would begin from Day 1. 

Example 3: Resident C is admitted to the SNF on 11/07/19. They are admitted to a hospital on 11/20/19. They return to the same SNF on 11/22/19. Because Resident C is admitted to the same SNF within three days from the point of discharge, this would be considered a continuation of the previous stay. No 5-Day assessment would be required upon readmission, though the IPA would be an option. Additionally, the variable per diem would continue from Day 14 (Day of Discharge). 

###### **Resident Discharged from Part A Skilled Services and Returns to SNF Part A Skilled Level Services** 

In the situation in which a resident is discharged from SNF Medicare Part A services and later requires SNF Part A skilled level of care services, and it is not an instance of an interrupted stay (as described above), the resident may be eligible for Medicare Part A SNF coverage if the following criteria are met: 

1. Less than 30 days have elapsed since the last day on which SNF level of care services were required and received, 

**October 2025** 

**Page 6-51** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**CH 6: Medicare SNF PPS** 

2. SNF-level services required by the resident are for a condition that was treated during the qualifying hospital stay or for a condition that arose while receiving care in the SNF for a condition for which the beneficiary was previously treated in the hospital, 

3. Services must be reasonable and necessary, 

4. Services can only be provided on an inpatient basis, 

5. Resident must require and receive the services on a daily basis, and 

6. Resident has remaining days in the SNF benefit period. 

For greater detail, refer to the **Medicare Benefit Policy Manual** , Chapter 8. 

###### **6.8 Non-compliance with the SNF PPS Assessment Schedule** 

To receive payment under the SNF PPS, the SNF must complete scheduled and unscheduled assessments as described in Chapter 2. 

According to 42 CFR 413.343, an assessment that does not have an ARD within the prescribed ARD window will be paid at the default rate for the number of days the ARD is out of compliance. Frequent late assessment scheduling practices or missing assessments may result in additional review. The default rate (ZZZZZ) takes the place of the otherwise applicable Federal rate. It is equal to the sum of the rate paid for the case-mix group reflecting the lowest acuity level under each PDPM component, and would generally be lower than the Medicare rate payable if the SNF had submitted an assessment in accordance with the prescribed assessment schedule. 

###### **Late Assessment** 

If the SNF fails to set the ARD within the defined ARD window for a PPS assessment, and the resident is still on Part A, the SNF must complete a late assessment. The ARD can be no earlier than the day the error was identified. 

The SNF will bill the default rate for the number of days that the assessment is out of compliance. This is equal to the number of days between the day following the last day of the available ARD window and the late ARD (including the late ARD). **The SNF would then bill the Health Insurance Prospective Payment System (HIPPS) code established by the late assessment for the remaining period of time that the assessment would have controlled payment.** For example, a 5-Day assessment with an ARD of Day 11 is out of compliance for 3 days and therefore would be paid at the default rate for Days 1 through 3 and the HIPPS code from the late 5-Day assessment for the remainder of the Part A stay, unless an IPA is completed. In the case of a late assessment, the variable per diem schedule still begins on Day 1 of the stay and not with the late assessment ARD and default billing will be assessed prior to billing based on the late 5-Day assessment. 

**October 2025** 

**Page 6-52** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**CH 6: Medicare SNF PPS** 

###### **Missed Assessment** 

If the SNF fails to set the ARD of a PPS assessment prior to the end of the last day of the ARD window, and the resident is no longer a SNF Part A resident, and as a result a PPS assessment does not exist in iQIES for the payment period, the provider may not usually bill for days when an assessment does not exist in iQIES. When a PPS assessment does not exist in iQIES, there is not a HIPPS code the provider may bill. In order to bill for Medicare SNF Part A services, the provider must submit a valid PPS assessment that is accepted into iQIES. The provider must bill the HIPPS code that is verified by the system. If the resident was already discharged from Medicare Part A when this is discovered, a PPS assessment may not be performed. 

However, there are instances when the SNF may bill the default code when a PPS assessment does not exist in iQIES. These exceptions are: 

1. The stay is less than 8 days within a spell of illness, 

2. The SNF is notified on an untimely basis of or is unaware of a Medicare Secondary Payer denial, 

3. The SNF is notified on an untimely basis of a beneficiary’s enrollment in Medicare Part A, 

4. The SNF is notified on an untimely basis of the revocation of a payment ban, 

5. The beneficiary requests a demand bill, or 

6. The SNF is notified on an untimely basis or is unaware of a beneficiary’s disenrollment from a Medicare Advantage plan. 

###### **ARD Outside the Medicare Part A SNF Benefit** 

A SNF may not use a date outside the SNF Part A Medicare Benefit (i.e., 100 days) as the ARD for a PPS assessment. For example, the resident returns to the SNF on December 11 following a hospital stay, requires and receives SNF skilled services (and meets all other required coverage criteria), and has 3 days left in their SNF benefit period. The SNF must set the ARD for the PPS assessment on December 11, 12, or 13 to bill for the HIPPS code associated with the assessment.

|**Dually Certified**<br>**Facilities**||Nursing facilities that participate in both the Medicare<br>and Medicaid programs.|



**October 2025** 

**Appendix A-6** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**Appendix A: Glossary and Common Acronyms** 

|**Term**|**Abbreviation**|**Definition**|
|---|---|---|
|**Duplicate Record**<br>**Error**||A fatal record error that results from a resubmission of a<br>record previously accepted into the CMS MDS database.<br>A duplicate record is identified as having the same target<br>date, reason for assessment, resident, and facility. This is<br>the only fatal record error that does not require correction<br>and resubmission.|
|**Electronic Health**<br>**Record**|**EHR**|An electronic version of a resident’s medical history that<br>is maintained by the provider over time. Sometimes<br>referred to as an electronic medical record (EMR).|
|**Electronic Medical**<br>**Record**|**EMR**|See Electronic Health Record.|
|**Entry Date**||The initial date of admission/entry to the facility, or the<br>date on which the resident most recently re-entered the<br>facility after being discharged (whether or not the return<br>was anticipated).|
|**Epilepsy**||A chronic neurological disorder that is characterized by<br>recurrent unprovoked seizures, as a result of abnormal<br>neuronal activity in the brain.|
|**External Catheter**||Device attached to the shaft of the penis like a condom, a<br>female external catheter, or other non-invasive urine<br>output management device or system that routes urine to<br>a drainage bag.|
|**Facility ID**|**FAC_ID**|The facility identification number is assigned to each<br>facility. The FAC_ID must be placed in the individual<br>MDS and tracking form records. This normally is<br>completed as a function within the facility’s MDS data<br>entry software.|
|**Fall**||Unintentional change in position coming to rest on the<br>ground_, floor,_or onto the next lower surface (e.g., onto a<br>bed, chair, or bedside mat)_or the result of an_<br>_overwhelming external force (e.g., a resident pushes_<br>_another resident)_.|
|**Fatal File Error**||An error in the MDS file format that causes the entire file<br>to be rejected. The individual records are not validated nor<br>stored in the database. The facility must contact its<br>software support to resolve the problem with the<br>submission file.|



**October 2025** 

**Appendix A-7** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**Appendix A: Glossary and Common Acronyms** 

|**Term**<br>**Abbreviation**|**Definition**|
|---|---|
|**Fatal Record Error**|An error in MDS record that is severe enough to result in<br>record rejection. A fatal record is not saved in the CMS<br>database. The facility must correct the error that caused<br>the rejection and resubmit a corrected original record.|
|**Fecal Impaction**|A mass of dry, hard stool that can develop in the rectum<br>due to chronic constipation. Watery stool from higher in<br>the bowel or irritation from the impaction may move<br>around the mass and leak out, causing soiling, often a sign<br>of a fecal impaction.|
|**Federal Register**|The official daily publication for rules, proposed rules,<br>and notices of Federal agencies and organizations, as well<br>as Executive Orders and other Presidential Documents. It<br>is a publication of the National Archives and Records<br>Administration and is available by subscription and<br>online.|
|**Feeding Tube**|Presence of any type of tube that can deliver<br>food/nutritional substances/fluids directly into the<br>gastrointestinal system. Examples include, but are not<br>limited to: nasogastric tubes, gastrostomy tubes,<br>jejunostomy tubes, percutaneous endoscopic gastrotomy<br>(PEG) tubes.|
|**Fever**|A fever is present when the resident’s temperature (°F) is<br>2.4 degrees greater than the baseline temperature.|
|**Final Validation**<br>**Report**<br>**FVR**|A report generated after the successful submission of<br>MDS 3.0 assessment data. This report lists all of the<br>residents for whom assessments have been submitted in a<br>particular submission batch and displays all errors and/or<br>warnings that occurred during the validation process. An<br>FVR is a facility’s documentation for successful file<br>submission. An individual record listed on the FVR<br>marked as “accepted” is documentation for successful<br>record submission.|
|**First Time in This**<br>**Facility**|Newly admitted resident who has not been admitted to this<br>facility before.|
|**F-Tag**|Numerical designations for criteria reviewed during the<br>nursing facility survey.|



**October 2025** 

**Appendix A-8** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**Appendix A: Glossary and Common Acronyms** 

|**Term**|**Abbreviation**|**Definition**|
|---|---|---|
|**Functional**<br>**Limitation in**<br>**Range of Motion**||Limited ability to move a joint that interferes with daily<br>functioning (particularly with activities of daily living) or<br>places the resident at risk of injury.|
|**Gradual Dose**<br>**Reduction**|**GDR**|Step-wise tapering of a dose to determine whether or not<br>symptoms, conditions, or risks can be managed by a lower<br>dose or whether or not the dose or medication can be<br>discontinued.|
|**Group Home**||A noninstitutional community residential setting that<br>includes services of the following types: home health<br>services, homemaker/personal care services, or meal<br>services.|
|**Habit Training/**<br>**Scheduled**<br>**Voiding**||A behavior technique that calls for scheduled toileting at<br>regular intervals on a planned basis to match the resident’s<br>voiding habits or needs.|
|**Hallucination**||A perception in a conscious and awake state, of something<br>in the absence of external stimuli. May be auditory or<br>visual or involve smells, tastes, or touch.|
|**Health Information**<br>**Exchange**|**HIE**|An organization that oversees and governs the exchange<br>of health-related information among organizations<br>according to nationally recognized standards. HIEs can<br>function at the federal, state and local level.|
|**Healthcare**<br>**Common**<br>**Procedure Coding**<br>**System**|**HCPCS**|A uniform coding system that describes medical services,<br>procedures, products, and supplies. These codes are used<br>primarily for billing.|
|**Health Insurance**<br>**Portability and**<br>**Accountability**<br>**Act of 1996**|**HIPAA**|Federal law that gives the Department of Health & Human<br>Services (HHS) the authority to mandate regulations that<br>govern privacy, security, and electronic transactions<br>standards for health care information.|
|**Health Insurance**<br>**Prospective**<br>**Payment System**<br>**Code**|**HIPPS**<br>**Code**|The Health Insurance Prospective Payment System code is<br>comprised of the PDPM case mix code, which is<br>calculated from the assessment data. The first four<br>positions of the HIPPS code contain the PDPM<br>classification codes for each PDPM component to be<br>billed for Medicare reimbursement, followed by an<br>indicator of the type of assessment that was completed.|



**October 2025** 

**Appendix A-9** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**Appendix A: Glossary and Common Acronyms** 

|**Term**|**Abbreviation**|**Definition**|
|---|---|---|
|**Health Literacy**||The degree to which individuals have the capacity to<br>obtain, process, and understand basic health information<br>and services needed to make appropriate health decisions.|
|**Hospice Services**||A program for terminally ill persons where an array of<br>services is provided for the palliation and management of<br>terminal illness and related conditions. The hospice must<br>be licensed by the state as a hospice provider and/or<br>certified under the Medicare program as a hospice<br>provider.|
|**Ileostomy**||A stoma that has been constructed by bringing the end or<br>loop of small intestine (the ileum) out onto the surface of<br>the skin.|
|**Inactivation**||A type of correction allowed under the MDS Correction<br>Policy. When an invalid record has been accepted into the<br>CMS database, a correction record is submitted with<br>inactivation selected as the type of correction. An<br>inactivation will remove the invalid record from the<br>database.|
|**Inattention**||Reduced ability to maintain attention to external stimuli<br>and to appropriately shift attention to new external stimuli.|
|**Indication**||The identified, documented clinical rationale for<br>administering a medication that is based upon a<br>physician’s (or prescriber’s) assessment of a resident’s<br>condition and therapeutic goals.|
|**Indwelling**<br>**Catheter**||A catheter that is maintained within the bladder for the<br>purpose of continuous drainage of urine.|
|**Interdisciplinary**<br>**Team**|**IDT**|A team that includes staff members from multiple<br>disciplines such as nursing, therapy, physicians, and other<br>advanced practitioners.|
|**_Interim Payment_**<br>**_Assessment_**|**_IPA_**|_An optional assessment that may be completed by_<br>_providers in order to report a change in the resident’s_<br>_PDPM classification._|
|**Intermittent**<br>**Catheterization**||Insertion and removal of a catheter through the urethra<br>into the bladder for bladder drainage.|



**October 2025** 

**Appendix A-10** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**Appendix A: Glossary and Common Acronyms** 

|**Term**|**Abbreviation**|**Definition**|
|---|---|---|
|**International**<br>**Classification**<br>**of Diseases –**<br>**Clinical**<br>**Modification**|**ICD-CM**|Official system of assigning codes to diagnoses and<br>procedures associated with hospital utilization in the<br>United States. The ICD-CM contains a numerical list of<br>the disease code numbers in tabular form, an alphabetical<br>index to the disease entries, and a classification system for<br>surgical, diagnostic, and therapeutic procedures.|
|**Internet Quality**<br>**Improvement and**<br>**Evaluation System**|**iQIES**|The umbrella system that encompasses the MDS system<br>and other provider-specific assessment collection systems,<br>as well as survey and certification data collection and<br>storage. SNF/NF providers not utilizing proprietary<br>software can complete and submit the MDS records in<br>iQIES, as well as obtain MDS-related reports.|
|**Interoperability**||A system’s ability to exchange electronic health<br>information with, and use electronic information from,<br>other systems without special effort on the part of the user.<br>Interoperability is further specified as health systems’<br>ability to electronically send health information to, receive<br>health information from, find health information in,<br>integrate health information into, or health information<br>from other electronic systems outside of their<br>organizations.|
|**Interrupted Stay**||Interrupted Stay is a Medicare Part A SNF stay in which a<br>resident is discharged from SNF care (i.e., the resident is<br>discharged from a Medicare Part A-covered stay) and<br>subsequently resumes SNF care in the**same**SNF for a<br>Medicare Part A-covered stay during the interruption<br>window.|



**October 2025** 

**Appendix A-11** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**Appendix A: Glossary and Common Acronyms** 

|**Term**|**Abbreviation**|**Definition**|
|---|---|---|
|**Interruption**<br>**Window**||The interruption window is a 3-day period, starting with<br>the calendar day of discharge and including the 2<br>immediately following calendar days. In other words, if a<br>resident in a Medicare Part A SNF stay is discharged from<br>Part A, the resident must resume Part A services, or return<br>to the**same**SNF (if physically discharged) to resume Part<br>A services, by 11:59 p.m. at the end of the third calendar<br>day after their Part A-covered stay ended. The interruption<br>window begins with the first non-covered day following a<br>Part A-covered stay and ends at 11:59 p.m. on the third<br>consecutive non-covered day following a Part A-covered<br>SNF stay. If these conditions are met, the subsequent stay<br>is considered a continuation of the previous Medicare Part<br>A-covered stay for the purposes of both the variable per<br>diem schedule and PPS assessment completion.|
|**Invalid Record**||As defined by the MDS Correction Policy, a record that<br>was accepted into iQIES that should not have been<br>submitted. Invalid records are defined as: a test record<br>submitted as production, a record for an event that did not<br>occur, a record with the wrong resident identified or the<br>wrong reason for assessment, or submission of an<br>inappropriate non-required record.|
|**Item Set Code**|**ISC**|A code based upon combinations of reasons for<br>assessment (A0310 items) that determines which items are<br>active on a particular type of MDS assessment or tracking<br>record.|
|**Leave of Absence**|**LOA**|Leave of Absence (LOA), which does not require<br>completion of either a Discharge assessment or an Entry<br>tracking record, occurs when a resident has a:<br>•<br>Temporary home visit of at least one night; or<br>•<br>Therapeutic leave of at least one night; or<br>•<br>Hospital observation stay less than 24 hours and<br>the hospital does not admit the resident.|
|**Legal Name**||Resident’s name as it appears on the Medicare card. If the<br>resident is not enrolled in the Medicare program, use the<br>resident’s name as it appears on a government-issued<br>document (i.e., driver’s license, birth certificate, social<br>security card).|



**October 2025** 

**Appendix A-12** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**Appendix A: Glossary and Common Acronyms** 

|**Term**<br>**Abbreviation**<br>**Definition**|
|---|
|**Level of**<br>**Consciousness**<br>Alert: startles easily to any sound or touch.<br>Drowsy/Lethargic: repeatedly dozes off when you are<br>asking questions but responds to voice or touch.<br>Stuporous: very difficult to arouse and keep aroused for<br>the interview.<br>Comatose: cannot be aroused despite shaking and<br>shouting.|
|**Look-Back Period**<br>See Observation Period.|
|**Major Surgery**<br>Generally, major surgery refers to a procedure that meets<br>the following criteria:<br>1. The resident was an inpatient in an acute care hospital<br>for at least 1 day in the 100 days prior to admission to<br>the skilled nursing facility (SNF),**and**<br>2. The surgery carried some degree of risk to the<br>resident’s life or the potential for severe disability.|
|**Makes Self**<br>**Understood**<br>Able to express or communicate requests, needs, opinions,<br>and to conduct social conversation in their primary<br>language, whether in speech, writing, sign language,<br>gestures, or a combination of these. Deficits in ability to<br>make one’s self understood (expressive communication<br>deficits) can include reduced voice volume and difficulty<br>in producing sounds, or difficulty in finding the right<br>word, making sentences, writing, and/or gesturing.|
|**MDS Completion**<br>**Date**<br>The date at which the RN assessment coordinator attests<br>that all portions of the MDS have been completed. This is<br>the date recorded at Z0500B.|
|**Mechanically**<br>**Altered Diet**<br>A diet specifically prepared to alter the texture or<br>consistency of food in order to facilitate oral intake.<br>Examples include soft solids, pureed foods, ground meat,<br>and thickened liquids.|
|**Medicaid**<br>A Federal and State program subject to the provisions of<br>Title XIX of the Social Security Act that pays for specific<br>kinds of medical care and treatment for low-income<br>families.|



**October 2025** 

**Appendix A-13** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**Appendix A: Glossary and Common Acronyms** 

|**Term**<br>**Abbreviation**|**Definition**|
|---|---|
|**Medicare**|A health insurance program administered by CMS under<br>provisions of Title XVIII of the Social Security Act for<br>people aged 65 and over, for those who have permanent<br>kidney failure, and for certain people with disabilities.<br>Medicare Part A: The part of Medicare that covers<br>inpatient hospital services and services furnished by other<br>institutional health care providers, such as nursing<br>facilities, home health agencies, and hospices.<br>Medicare Part B: The part of Medicare that covers<br>services of doctors, suppliers of medical items and<br>services, and various types of outpatient services.|
|**Medicare**<br>**Administrative**<br>**Contractor**<br>**MAC**|An organization designated by CMS to process Medicare<br>claims for payment that are submitted by a nursing<br>facility. MACs were previously called Fiscal<br>Intermediaries (FIs).|
|**Medicare-Covered**<br>**Stay**|Skilled Nursing Facility stays billable to Medicare Part A.<br>Does not include stays billable to other payers (e.g.,<br>Medicare Advantage plans).|
|**Medicare Number**|An identifier assigned to an individual for participation in<br>national health insurance program. The Medicare Health<br>Insurance identifier is different from the resident’s Social<br>Security Number (SSN) and may contain both letters and<br>numbers.|
|**Medication**<br>**Interaction**|The impact of medication or other substance (such as<br>nutritional supplements including herbal products, food, or<br>substances used in diagnostic studies) upon another<br>medication. The interactions may alter absorption,<br>distribution, metabolism, or elimination. These<br>interactions may decrease the effectiveness of the<br>medication or increase the potential for adverse<br>consequences.|
|**Minimum Data**<br>**Set**<br>**MDS**|A core set of screening, clinical assessment, and<br>functional status elements, including common definitions<br>and coding categories that form the foundation of the<br>comprehensive assessment for all residents of long-term<br>care facilities certified to participate in Medicare and<br>Medicaid and for patients receiving SNF services in non-<br>critical access hospitals with a swing bed agreement.|



**October 2025** 

**Appendix A-14** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**Appendix A: Glossary and Common Acronyms** 

|**Term**|**Abbreviation**|**Definition**|
|---|---|---|
|**Modification**||A type of correction allowed under the MDS Correction<br>Policy. A modification is required when a valid MDS<br>record has been accepted by the CMS MDS database, but<br>the information in the record contains errors. The<br>modification will correct the record in the CMS database.<br>A modification is not done when a record has been<br>rejected.|
|**Monitoring**||The ongoing collection and analysis of information (such<br>as observations and diagnostic test results) and<br>comparison to baseline and current data in order to<br>ascertain the individual’s response to treatment and care,<br>including progress or lack of progress toward a goal.<br>Monitoring can detect any improvements, complications<br>or adverse consequences of the condition or of the<br>treatments; and support decisions about adding,<br>modifying, continuing, or discontinuing, any<br>interventions.|
|**Most Recent**<br>**Medicare Stay**||This is a Medicare Part A covered stay that has started on<br>or after the most recent admission/entry or reentry to the<br>nursing facility.|
|**Music Therapy**||Music therapy is an intervention that uses music to address<br>physical, emotional, cognitive, and social needs of<br>individuals of all ages. Music therapy interventions can be<br>designed to promote wellness, manage stress, alleviate<br>pain, express feelings, enhance memory, improve<br>communication, and promote physical rehabilitation. In<br>order for music therapy to be coded on the MDS, the<br>service must be provided or directly supervised by a<br>qualified staff.|
|**National Drug**<br>**Code**|**NDC**|A unique 10-digit number assigned to each drug product<br>listed under Section 510 of the Federal Food, Drug and<br>Cosmetic Act. The NDC code identifies the vendor, drug<br>name, dosage, and form of the drug.|
|**National Provider**<br>**Identifier**|**NPI**|A unique federal number that identifies providers of health<br>care services. The NPI applies to the SNF/NFs for all of<br>its residents.|
|**Nephrostomy**<br>**Tube**||A catheter inserted through the skin into the kidney or its<br>collecting system.|



**October 2025** 

**Appendix A-15** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**Appendix A: Glossary and Common Acronyms** 

|**Term**<br>**Abbreviation**|**Definition**|
|---|---|
|**Non-medication**<br>**Pain Intervention**|An intervention, other than medication, used to try to<br>manage pain which may include, but are not limited to:<br>bio-feedback, application of heat/cold, massage, physical<br>therapy,_occupational therapy,_ nerve block, stretching and<br>strengthening exercises, chiropractic, electrical<br>stimulation, radiotherapy, ultrasound, and acupuncture.|
|**Non-**<br>**pharmacological**<br>**Intervention**|Approaches that do not involve the use of medication to<br>address a medical condition.|
|**_Non-Therapy_**<br>**_Ancillary_**<br>**_NTA_**|_One of the five categories used to determine_<br>_reimbursement under PDPM. NTA accounts for the non-_<br>_therapy services and treatments a resident may need_<br>_during their stay, such as medications, medical supplies,_<br>_and specialized treatments._|
|**Nursing Facility**<br>**NF**|A facility that is primarily engaged in providing skilled<br>nursing care and related services to individuals who<br>require medical or nursing care or rehabilitation services<br>for the rehabilitation of injured, disabled, or sick persons,<br>or on a regular basis, health related care services above the<br>level of custodial care to other than mentally retarded<br>individuals.|
|**Nursing**<br>**Monitoring**|Nursing Monitoring includes clinical monitoring by a<br>licensed nurse (e.g. serial blood pressure evaluations,<br>medication management, etc.).|
|**Nutrition or**<br>**Hydration**<br>**Intervention to**<br>**Manage Skin**<br>**Problems**|Interventions related to diet, nutrients, and hydration that<br>are provided to prevent or manage specific skin conditions<br>(e.g., wheat-free diet to prevent dermatitis, increased<br>calorie diets to meet basic standards for daily energy<br>requirements, vitamin or mineral supplements for<br>specifically identified deficiencies.)|
|**Observation Period**|The time period over which an MDS assessment captures<br>a resident’s condition or status. A day begins at 12:00 a.m.<br>and ends at 11:59 p.m.; the observation period must also<br>cover this time period. An MDS assessment captures only<br>occurrences during the observation period. In other words,<br>if it did not occur during the observation period, it is not<br>coded on the MDS. Also referred to as**Look-Back Period**<br>or**Assessment Period**.|



**October 2025** 

**Appendix A-16** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**Appendix A: Glossary and Common Acronyms** 

|**Term**|**Abbreviation**|<br>**Definition**|
|---|---|---|
|**Occupational**<br>**Therapy**|**OT**|Services that are provided or directly supervised by a<br>licensed occupational therapist. A qualified occupational<br>therapy assistant may provide therapy but not supervise<br>others (aides or volunteers) giving therapy. Includes<br>services provided by a qualified occupational therapy<br>assistant who is employed by (or under contract to) the<br>nursing facility only if they are under the direction of a<br>licensed occupational therapist. Occupational therapist and<br>occupational therapy assistant are defined in regulations<br>(42 CFR 484.4). Occupational therapy interventions<br>address deficits in physical, cognitive, psychosocial,<br>sensory, and other aspects of performance in order to<br>support engagement in everyday life activities that affect<br>health, well-being, and quality of life.|
|**Omnibus Budget**<br>**Reconciliation Act**<br>**of 1987**|**OBRA ’87**|Law that enacted reforms in nursing facility care and<br>provides the statutory authority for the MDS. The goal is<br>to ensure that residents of nursing facilities receive quality<br>care that will help them to attain or maintain the highest<br>practicable, physical, mental, and psychosocial well-being.|
|**On Admission**||On admission is defined as: as close to the actual time of<br>admission as possible.|
|**Oral Lesions**||An abnormal area of tissue on the lips, gums, tongue,<br>palate, cheek lining, or throat. This may include<br>ulceration, plaques or patches (e.g. candidiasis), tumors or<br>masses, and color changes (red, white, yellow, or<br>darkened).|
|**Pain Medication**<br>**Regimen**||Pharmacological agent(s) prescribed to relieve or prevent<br>the recurrence of pain. Include all medications used for<br>pain management by any route and any frequency during<br>the look-back period.|
|**Passive Range of**<br>**Motion**|**_PROM_**|Movement within the unrestricted range of motion for a<br>segment, which is provided entirely by an external force.<br>There is no voluntary muscle contraction. This type of<br>range of motion is often used when a resident is not able<br>to perform the movement at all_or puts forth_no effort.|
|**Patient Health**<br>**Questionnaire**|**PHQ-2 to**<br>**9©**|A validated interview that screens for symptoms of<br>depression. It provides a standardized severity score and a<br>rating for evidence of a depressive disorder.|



**October 2025** 

**Appendix A-17** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**Appendix A: Glossary and Common Acronyms** 

|**Term**<br>**Abbreviatio**|**n**<br>**Definition**|
|---|---|
|**Patient Driven**<br>**Payment Model**<br>**PDPM**|The Patient Driven Payment Model (PDPM) is a new<br>case-mix classification system for classifying skilled<br>nursing facility (SNF) residents in a Medicare Part A<br>covered stay into payment groups under the SNF<br>Prospective Payment System. Effective beginning October<br>1, 2019, PDPM replaced the Federal case-mix<br>classification system, the Resource Utilization Group,<br>Version IV (RUG-IV).|
|**Persistent**<br>**Vegetative State**<br>**PVS**|PVS is an enduring situation in which an individual has<br>failed to demonstrate meaningful cortical function but can<br>sustain basic body functions supported by noncortical<br>brain activity.|
|**Physical Therapy**<br>**PT**|Services that are provided or directly supervised by a<br>licensed physical therapist. A qualified physical therapy<br>assistant_(PTA)_ may provide therapy but not supervise<br>others (aides or volunteers) giving therapy. Includes<br>services provided by a qualified physical therapy assistant<br>who is employed by (or under contract to) the nursing<br>facility only if they are under the direction of a licensed<br>physical therapist. Physical therapist and physical therapist<br>assistant are defined in regulation 42 CFR 484.4. Physical<br>therapists (PTs) are licensed health care professionals who<br>diagnose and manage movement dysfunction and enhance<br>physical and functional status for people of all ages. PTs<br>alleviate impairments and activity limitations and<br>participation restrictions, promote and maintain optimal<br>fitness, physical function, and quality of life, and reduce<br>risk as it relates to movement and health. Following an<br>evaluation of an individual with impairments, activity<br>limitations, and participation restrictions or other health-<br>related conditions, the physical therapist designs an<br>individualized plan of physical therapy care and services<br>for each patient. Physical therapists use a variety of<br>interventions to treat patients. Interventions may include<br>therapeutic exercise, functional training, manual therapy<br>techniques, assistive and adaptive devices and equipment,<br>physical agents, and electrotherapeutic modalities.|
|**Physician**<br>**Prescribed Weight-**<br>**loss Regimen**|A weight reduction plan ordered by the resident’s<br>physician with the care plan goal of weight reduction.<br>May employ a calorie-restricted diet or other weight-loss<br>diets and exercise. Also includes planned diuresis. It is<br>important that weight loss is intentional.|



**October 2025** 

**Appendix A-18** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**Appendix A: Glossary and Common Acronyms** 

|**Term**<br>**Abbreviation**|**Definition**|
|---|---|
|**Portal**|A secure online website that gives providers, residents,<br>and others 24-hour access to personal health information<br>from anywhere with an Internet connection.|
|**_Prior to the Benefit_**<br>**_of Services_**|_Prior to provision of any care by facility staff that would_<br>_result in more independent coding._|
|**Private Home/**<br>**Apartment**|A noninstitutional community residential setting that can<br>include houses, condominiums, or apartments in the<br>community whether owned by the resident or another<br>person, as well as retirement communities and<br>independent housing for the elderly.|
|**Program**<br>**Transmittal**|Transmittal pages summarize the instructions to providers,<br>emphasizing what has been changed, added, or clarified.<br>They provide background information that would be<br>useful in implementing the instructions. Program<br>Transmittals can be found at the following website:<br>_https://www.cms.gov/medicare/regulations-_<br>_guidance/transmittals_|
|**Prompted Voiding**|Prompted voiding is a behavioral intervention to maintain<br>or regain urinary continence and may include timed verbal<br>reminders and positive feedback for successful toileting.|
|**Prospective**<br>**Payment System**<br>**PPS**|A payment system, developed for Medicare skilled<br>nursing facilities, which pays facilities an all-inclusive rate<br>for all Medicare Part A beneficiary services. Payment is<br>determined by a case mix classification system that<br>categorizes patients by the type and intensity of resources<br>used.|
|**Psychological**<br>**Therapy**|The treatment of mental and emotional disorders through<br>the use of psychological techniques designed to encourage<br>communication of conflicts and insight into problems,<br>with the goal being relief of symptoms, changes in<br>behavior leading to improved social and vocational<br>functioning, and personality growth. Psychological<br>therapy may be provided by a psychiatrist, psychologist,<br>clinical social worker, or clinical nurse specialist in mental<br>health as allowable under applicable state laws.|
|**Psychomotor**<br>**Retardation**|Visibly slowed level of activity or mental processing in<br>residents who are alert. Psychomotor retardation should be<br>differentiated from altered level of consciousness (i.e.<br>stupor) and lethargy.|

By<br>serving regions of two to six states each, QIN-QIOs are<br>able to help best practices for better care spread more<br>quickly, while still accommodating local conditions and<br>cultural factors.|

Their mission is to ensure<br>the quality, effectiveness, efficiency, and economy of<br>health care services provided to Medicare beneficiaries.|

|**Recreational**<br>**Therapy**||Services that are provided or directly supervised by a<br>qualified recreational therapist who holds a national<br>certification in recreational therapy, also referred to as a<br>“Certified Therapeutic Recreation Specialist.”<br>Recreational therapy includes, but is not limited to,<br>providing treatment services and recreation activities to<br>individuals using a variety of techniques, including arts<br>and crafts, animals, sports, games, dance and movement,<br>drama, music, and community outings. Recreation<br>therapists treat and help maintain the physical, mental, and<br>emotional well-being of their clients by seeking to reduce<br>depression, stress, and anxiety; recover basic motor<br>functioning and reasoning abilities; build confidence; and<br>socialize effectively. Recreational therapists should not be<br>confused with recreation workers, who organize<br>recreational activities primarily for enjoyment.|

These services or<br>programs can include, for example, physical therapy,<br>occupational therapy, speech therapy, and cardiac and<br>pulmonary therapies.|
|**Religion**||Belief in and reverence for a supernatural power or powers<br>regarded as creator and governor of the universe. Can be<br>expressed in practice of rituals associated with various<br>religious faiths, attendance and participation in religious<br>services, or in private prayer or religious study.|

**Appendix C-1** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**Appendix C: CAA Resources** 

Chapter 4 of this manual provides information on specific care areas triggered and the CAA process. This appendix contains both specific and general resources that nursing homes may choose to use to further assess care areas triggered from the MDS 3.0 Resident Assessment Instrument (RAI). The resources include the care area specific tools beginning in this section and the general resource list at the end of this appendix. 

It is important to note that the resources provided in this appendix are provided solely as a courtesy for use by nursing homes, should they choose to, in completing the RAI CAA process. **<u>It is also important to reiterate that CMS does not mandate, nor does it endorse, the use of any particular resource(s), including those provided in this appendix.</u>** However, nursing homes should ensure that the resource(s) used are current, evidence-based or expert-endorsed research and clinical practice guidelines/resources. 

**_DISCLAIMER:_ The list of resources in this appendix is neither prescriptive nor allinclusive. References to non-U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) sources or sites on the Internet are provided as a service and do not constitute or imply endorsement of these organizations or their programs by CMS or HHS. CMS is not responsible for the content of pages found at these sites. URL addresses were current as of the date of this publication.** 

**October 2025** 

**Appendix C-2** 

**CMS’s RAI Version 3.0 Manual** 

**Appendix C: CAA Resources** 

###### **CARE AREA SPECIFIC RESOURCES** 

The specific resources or tools contained on the next several pages are provided by care area. The general instructions for using them include: 

Step 1: After completing the MDS, review all MDS items and responses to determine if any care areas have been triggered. 

Step 2: For any triggered care area(s), conduct a thorough assessment of the resident using the care area-specific resources. 

Step 3: Check the box in the left column if the item is present for this resident. **_Some of this information will be on the MDS - some will not._** 

Step 4: In the right column the facility can provide a summary of supporting documentation regarding the basis or reason for checking a particular item or items. This could include the location and date of that information, symptoms, possible causal and contributing factor(s) for item(s) checked, etc. 

Step 5: Obtain and consider input from resident and/or family/resident’s representative regarding the care area. 

Step 6: Analyze the findings in the context of their relationship to the care area and standards of practice. This should include a review of indicators and supporting documentation, including symptoms and causal and contributing factors, related to this care area. Draw conclusions about the causal/contributing factors and effect(s) on the resident, and document these conclusions in the Analysis of Findings section. 

Step 7: Decide whether referral to other disciplines is warranted and document this decision. 

Step 8: In the Care Plan Considerations section, document whether a care plan for the triggered care area will be developed and the reason(s) why or why not. 

Step 9: Information in the _Supporting Documentation_ column can be used to populate the _Location and Date of CAA Documentation_ column in Section V, Item V0200A (CAA Results) – for e.g. “See Delirium CAA 4/30/11, H&P dated 4/18/11.” 

_NOTE: An optional Signature/Date line has been added to each checklist. This was added if the facility wants to document the staff member who completed the checklist and date completed._ 

**_DISCLAIMER:_ The checklists of care area specific resources in this appendix are not mandated, prescriptive, or all-inclusive and are provided as a service to facilities. They do not constitute or imply endorsement by CMS or HHS.**

Where rehabilitation goals are envisioned, use of the **_ADL Supplement_** will help care planners to focus on those areas that might be improved, allowing them to choose from among a number of basic tasks in designated areas. Part 1 of the supplement can assist in the evaluation of all residents that trigger this care area. Part 2 of the supplement can be helpful for residents with rehabilitation potential (ADL Triggers A), to help plan a treatment program.

**Appendix C: CAA Resources 16. Pressure Ulcer/Injury** 

###### **16. PRESSURE ULCER/INJURY** 

###### **<u>Review of Indicators of Pressure Ulcer/Injury</u>** 

||<br>**Existing pressure ulcer/injury**(M0210,<br>M0300)|<br>**Supporting Documentation**<br>**(Basis/reason for checking the item,**<br>**including the location, date, and source**<br>**(if applicable) of that information)**|
|---|---|---|
|~~□~~|• Assess location, size, stage, presence and type<br>of drainage, presence of odors, condition of<br>surrounding skin<br> Note if eschar or slough is present<br>(M0300F)<br> Assess for signs of infection, such as the<br>presence of a foul odor, increasing pain,<br>surrounding skin is reddened (erythema)<br>or warm, or there is a presence of<br>purulent drainage<br> Note whether granulation tissue (required<br>for healing) is present and the wound is<br>healing as expected|**Blank**|
|~~□~~|• If the ulcer/injury does not show signs of<br>healing despite treatment, consider<br>complicating factors<br> Elevated bacterial level in the absence of<br>clinical infection<br> Presence of exudate, necrotic debris or<br>slough in the wound, too much granula-<br>tion tissue, or odor in the wound bed<br> Underlyingosteomyelitis(bone infection)||
||<br>**Extrinsic risk factors**|**Supporting Documentation**|
|~~□~~|• Pressure<br> Requires staff assistance to move<br>sufficiently to relieve pressure over any<br>one site<br> Confined to a bed or chair all or most of<br>the time<br> Needs special mattress or seat cushion to<br>reduce or relieve pressure (M1200A,<br>M1200B)<br> Requires regular schedule of turning<br>(M1200C)|**Blank**|
|~~□~~|• Friction and shear<br> Slides down in the bed<br> Moved by sliding rather than lifting||
|~~□~~|• Maceration<br> Persistently wet, especially from fecal<br>incontinence, wound drainage, or<br>perspiration<br> Moisture associated skin damage<br>(M1040H)||



(continued)
